abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel theoretical framework termed Semantic Entanglement Theory (SET) for knowledge graph representation learning, fundamentally redefining how semantic relationships are modeled in knowledge systems. Unlike conventional knowledge graph embedding approaches that treat entities and relations independently, SET conceptualizes knowledge acquisition as an entanglement process where semantic coherence emerges from iterative information integration across multiple ontological layers. The theoretical foundations of SET are rigorously established through formal proofs demonstrating that optimal knowledge representation requires simultaneous optimization of both local semantic consistency and global topological structure. We derive mathematical bounds showing that SET achieves information-theoretic optimality in capturing complex relational patterns that traditional tensor factorization methods cannot express. Extensive experiments on benchmark knowledge graphs including FB15k-237 and WN18RR validate that SET outperforms existing paradigms by 12-18% in link prediction tasks. This work establishes a new research paradigm that shifts the focus from embedding geometry to semantic entanglement dynamics, opening promising avenues for understanding knowledge acquisition mechanisms in artificial intelligence systems.

We present a significant theoretical advancement in information retrieval through the development of Adaptive Semantic Decomposition (ASD), which substantially improves upon traditional probabilistic relevance models. The proposed framework addresses the fundamental limitation of existing retrieval models in handling semantic vocabulary mismatch by introducing a hierarchical semantic decomposition mechanism that bridges the lexical and conceptual levels of relevance assessment. Through rigorous mathematical derivation, we prove that ASD achieves tighter theoretical bounds on retrieval effectiveness compared to standard language models, with an expected improvement of log(n) in the average precision metric where n represents the semantic vocabulary size. The framework incorporates a novel relevance propagation mechanism based on random walk theory with adaptive restart probabilities, which we theoretically analyze using spectral graph theory. Empirical evaluation on TREC collections demonstrates that ASD achieves statistically significant improvements of 15-23% over state-of-the-art neural retrieval models in terms of nDCG@10. This work provides both theoretical justification and practical algorithms for bridging the semantic gap in modern information retrieval systems.

This paper presents StreamChain, a groundbreaking distributed system architecture for real-time knowledge extraction from data streams that fundamentally reimagines the integration of stream processing and blockchain technology. The system introduces a novel triple-store architecture combining in-memory graph processing, append-only semantic logs, and decentralized knowledge consensus to achieve unprecedented levels of data quality and trustworthiness in continuous knowledge discovery. StreamChain's core innovation lies in its Adaptive Semantic Window mechanism that dynamically adjusts temporal aggregation horizons based on concept drift detection, enabling context-aware knowledge extraction from non-stationary data streams. The system's consensus protocol achieves sub-second latency through a novel Proof-of-Knowledge mechanism that validates extracted facts against historical semantic patterns without requiring energy-intensive mining operations. We deployed StreamChain in a production environment processing 2.5 million events per second from IoT sensor networks, demonstrating 99.97% knowledge accuracy and 47ms average extraction latency. The system maintains consistent performance during concept drift scenarios, with less than 3% degradation compared to 28% observed in baseline stream mining approaches.

We design and implement DeepTextMiner, a high-performance text mining system that substantially advances the state-of-the-art in automated knowledge extraction from unstructured documents. The system architecture introduces a novel Multi-Granularity Attention Network (MGAN) that processes text simultaneously at character, word, sentence, and document levels, enabling comprehensive semantic pattern recognition across heterogeneous text corpora. Our engineering contributions include a distributed inference pipeline utilizing asynchronous batching and intelligent caching strategies that achieve 340% throughput improvement over existing neural NLP systems while maintaining extraction quality. DeepTextMiner incorporates a Domain Adaptation Module that enables rapid deployment to new subject areas through transfer learning with only 500 labeled examples, reducing domain adaptation costs by an order of magnitude. We conducted extensive evaluation across six diverse domains including biomedical literature, legal documents, and technical reports, demonstrating consistent F1 improvements of 8-14% over previous systems. The system successfully extracted over 12 million structured facts from a corpus of 2 million research papers within 18 hours using commodity hardware, validating its practical scalability for big data analytics applications.
